question: Following the Commission’s answer to question E-000244/2024 on the removal of EUfunded cycle lanes in Logroño, doubts remain as to the proper use of investments linked to the Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF) in this city.

Component 1 of the Spanish recovery plan provides for investments to promote sustainable mobility and reduce urban emissions, objectives which could be compromised by local decisions reversing actions financed by European funds.

Furthermore, consideration of the petition submitted to the European Parliament’s Committee on Petitions on this matter is at a standstill owing to its obstruction by the EPP and the extreme right, despite the concerns of local sustainable mobility and environmental protection groups. In light of the above: 1.
Is the Commission examining whether the decisions of Logroño City Council are compatible with the milestones and targets of component 1 of the Spanish RRF?

Can the Commission confirm whether it monitors the impact of this type of action on the achievement of sustainable urban mobility objectives in Spain, especially in projects co-financed with NextGenerationEU funds?
In the event that a deviation from the objectives of the approved projects were to be detected, what corrective measures could the Commission apply?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (12.2.2026) The full list of investments and reforms that Spain committed to undertake is set out in the Annex to the Council Implementing Decision of 13 July 2021 on the approval of the assessment of the recovery and resilience plan for Spain1.

The Commission identified the actions concerned by the question as potentially being part of target 9 which completion is planned by Q2 2026 and could be part of payment request seven which has not been submitted yet2. As a result, the Commission services have not received or examined evidence as regards this project, nor disbursed any funds.

Additionally, the Commission services have no assurance at this stage that the mobility project in Logroño will be proposed by Spain as eligible for Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF) funding under this target.

Should Spain put this project forward as contributing to the fulfilment of target 9, the Commission would assess the target against the requirements set out in the Annex to the Council Implementing Decision (CID).

In the context of a payment request, shall the Commission find that one or more targets are not satisfactory fulfilled, there is a possibility of adopting a partial payment suspension in line with the provisions of Article 24(6) of the RRF regulation3.

If as part of the seventh payment Spain submits more projects than those required by target 9 in the CID, the non-compliance of one with the requirements of target 9 in the CID would not automatically lead to the non-satisfactory fulfilment of the target.

pdf, target 9 has been moved from the sixth to the seventh payment request, while targets 5 and 6 have been removed from the Plan in line with the guidelines provided https://commission.europa.eu/document/download/ad5f00c94101-41a0-9d8f-e78f06c0c7ed_en?filename=COM_2025_310_1_EN_ACT_part1_v8.pdf. 3 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2021/241/oj/eng.
